title: pvVisItImageReader
body:
## pvVisItImageReader

Reads images through VisIt's Image plugin: PNM/PPM, Stimulate SDT/SPR and .imgvol image stacks. It offers two rectilinear meshes, "ImageMesh" with pixel values as cell data and "ImageMesh_nodal" with them as point data. For PNG, JPEG or TIFF series the native pvPNGSeriesReader, pvJPEGSeriesReader and pvTIFFSeriesReader give vtkImageData directly; pvImageReader handles headerless raw volumes. FileName takes a list of files, each one time step of a series (ParaView's file-series wrapper).

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Select the mesh that matches the arrays you want: cell arrays live on "ImageMesh" and *_nodal point arrays on "ImageMesh_nodal".
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- The VisIt plugin's own read options stay at their defaults; the ParaView proxy exposes no property to change them.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItImageReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItImageReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrayStatus` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from image data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The image plugin offers per-pixel channels; each is offered twice, as a cell array on "ImageMesh" and with the suffix _nodal as a point array on "ImageMesh_nodal"; colour formats add 4-component "color"/"color_nodal" arrays; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `MaterialStatus` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The image plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `MeshStatus` | Names of the image meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The Image plugin reports "ImageMesh" (pixels as cells) and "ImageMesh_nodal" (pixels as points); .imgvol files stack images into a 3-D volume. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrayStatus` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from image data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The image plugin offers per-pixel channels; each is offered twice, as a cell array on "ImageMesh" and with the suffix _nodal as a point array on "ImageMesh_nodal"; colour formats add 4-component "color"/"color_nodal" arrays; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItImageReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
